articles.description: The panelists explore how engineering teams adapt delivery architectures, pipelines, security, and governance for AI-assisted development. They share practical strategies for verifying AI-generated code, solving testing and deployment bottlenecks, maintaining human oversight, and measuring AI’s true impact on software velocity, quality, reliability, and operational cost.

articles.title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components
articles.summary: Microsoft has released ASP.NET Core in .NET 11. The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refre...
articles.description: Microsoft has released ASP.NET Core in .NET 11. The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refresh. Blazor gains a CacheView component, client-side validation for static SSR forms, opt-in circuit pause for inactive tabs, and experimental AI components. Zstandard compression is on by default.

articles.description: Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. Healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates. By Ben Linders

articles.description: Nicholas Matsakis shares why AI makes Rust the ideal choice for modern production systems, skipping steep adoption hurdles via compiler guardrails.
